Prepared at `2026-09-22T09:02:00+01:00`. **Drafts only: not published, scheduled or emailed.** Recheck inside the publication window. Cardiff and Birmingham direct Meta gates remain disabled; artwork has not yet been created or claimed ready.

The shortlist is intentionally compact. Current primary-source evidence supported four useful Cardiff ideas and three Birmingham ideas without padding the edition with unverified listings or a stack of routine library clubs.

## Cardiff research — weekend 26–27 September

1. **National Museum Cardiff** — Saturday and Sunday, 10:00–17:00; galleries close 16:45. General admission free; some exhibitions/activities may charge. A free advance day ticket is available but is not described as mandatory. Under-16s need an adult. Indoor; prams allowed. Visitor parking £6.50.
   - https://museum.wales/cardiff/visit/
2. **St Fagans National Museum of History** — Saturday and Sunday, 10:00–17:00. Entry free; parking £7. Under-16s need an adult. Historic outdoor site with uneven/slippery paths, slopes, steps and water; pushchairs enter only specified buildings. Picnics welcome.
   - https://museum.wales/stfagans/visit/
3. **Bute Park sculpture hunt** — park hours currently 07:30–18:45. More than 20 sculptures include a frog, beetle, snail, otter and salmon; several are designed for climbing/crawling. Free outdoor, self-led plan. The official page does not publish a child age band; grown-up supervision is essential around climbing pieces, paths and the river.
   - https://bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/
4. **Techniquest** — Saturday 26 September, 10:00–17:00; the live opening page does not yet list Sunday 27, so this draft promotes Saturday only. Capacity is limited; book ahead. Standard admission: adult £15.45, child 3–15 £13.63, under-3 free; family up to five £52.72. Donation-inclusive prices are higher.
   - https://www.techniquest.org/visit/opening-times-and-prices/

### Cardiff social caption — Friday roundup draft

Cardiff, pick your family mission: dinosaurs, experiments, wooden beasts or a whole village from the past. 🦖⚡🌳

Four plans for **Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 September**:

🦕 **DINOSAURS + ART** — National Museum Cardiff, 10am–5pm both days. General entry is free; under-16s need an adult. Some exhibitions cost extra.

🏡 **STEP INTO OLD WALES** — St Fagans, 10am–5pm both days. Free entry; parking £7. Bring a picnic and expect uneven paths, slopes and steps.

🐸 **FIND THE WOODEN CREATURES** — Bute Park has more than 20 sculptures, including a climbable frog, beetle and hollow log. Free and outdoors; keep close around climbing pieces and the river.

🧪 **PULL, PUSH, BUILD** — Techniquest is confirmed open **Saturday only**, 10am–5pm. Standard online prices: adult £15.45, child £13.63, under-3s free; book ahead because capacity is limited.

Save the list, check the links before travelling, then pick the one that fits your crew. 🧡

National Museum Cardiff and St Fagans are both free to enter and open 10am–5pm Saturday and Sunday. St Fagans charges £7 parking. Bute Park's self-led sculpture hunt is another free option, with more than 20 wooden creatures and seats to track down.

## Birmingham research — weekend 26–27 September

1. **Lapworth Museum of Geology** — Saturday and Sunday, 12:00–17:00. Free, no booking. Dinosaur, fossils, minerals and crystals. Wheelchair/pram accessible with lift; baby changing. Weekend campus parking £3/day.
   - https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/cultural-attractions/lapworth-museum-of-geology/visit-us
2. **Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery** — Saturday and Sunday, 10:00–17:00; last entry 16:45. Free general admission, no booking. Open areas include Wild City family gallery, Pre-Raphaelites, Staffordshire Hoard and Birmingham History; much of the building remains closed. Baby changing and disabled toilets available; picnic space is stairs-only.
   - https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/birmingham-museum-and-art-gallery/visit
3. **Thinktank** — Saturday and Sunday, 10:00–17:00; last admission 16:30. Pre-booking advised at busy weekends. Term-time admission: adult £18.95, child 3–15 £9.95, under-3 free, family up to four £45.95. Planetarium costs extra and can sell out. On-site £3 tickets after 16:00 provide only the final hour. Children 11 and under need a parent/guardian aged 16+.
   - https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/thinktank/visit
   - https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/thinktank/visit/tickets

### Birmingham social caption — Friday roundup draft

Birmingham: meet a dinosaur, explore a Wild City or spend the day pressing every science button in sight. 🦖🌿🚀

Three properly checked family options for **26–27 September**:

🦴 **FREE FOSSIL FIX** — Lapworth Museum, noon–5pm Saturday and Sunday. Dinosaurs, fossils, crystals and minerals; no booking. Pram/wheelchair access and baby changing. Campus parking is £3 for the day.

🐾 **FREE WILD CITY** — Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, 10am–5pm both days. No booking. The family gallery, Staffordshire Hoard and Birmingham History are open, but parts of the building remain closed.

🚀 **BIG SCIENCE DAY** — Thinktank, 10am–5pm both days. Term-time prices: adult £18.95, child £9.95, under-3s free; family ticket £45.95. Book ahead. Planetarium shows cost extra and may sell out.

Two free indoor adventures, plus one full-on paid science day. Save it for the weekend. 🧡
